attack_mechanism: The security-relevant dependency is `keccak.in -> keccak.padder_.in -> keccak.padder_out -> keccak.f_permutation_.round_.a[2][0] -> keccak.f_permutation_.round_.c[2][0]`. On the first calculation step after `accept`, the padded rate block has just been XORed into the persistent state and is being evaluated by the two-round Keccak network. `keccak.f_permutation_.round_.c[2][0]` is a theta-mixed lane before rho/pi relocation; its bits are deterministic functions of the newly accepted `keccak_in` block and the previous state. Probing `keccak.f_permutation_.round_.c[2][0]` in this early-round window exposes an internal representation before all 24 rounds have diffused the input. The observation leaks lane-level information about the secret input that is not present as a directly accessible architectural signal.

The security-relevant dependency is `keccak.in -> keccak.padder_.in -> keccak.padder_out -> keccak.f_permutation_.round_.a[2][0] -> keccak.f_permutation_.round_.c[2][0]`. On subsequent `calc` cycles, feedback from the registered permutation output re-enters the same combinational round network. `keccak.f_permutation_.round_.c[2][0]` is recomputed for later round pairs and therefore yields a time series of input-dependent values from a theta-mixed lane before rho/pi relocation. Sampling `keccak.f_permutation_.round_.c[2][0]` at a fixed cycle offset across repeated operations supplies aligned intermediate values for differential or correlation analysis. Combining those observations can recover secret-dependent relationships even when a single lane observation is insufficient to reconstruct the input.
